exposure: lower uterine anterior wall thickness (measured pre-delivery)
cohort: The study included 159 pregnant women with a scarred uterus undergoing repeat delivery between March 2022 and May 2024.
finding: Thinner lower uterine anterior wall thickness, single-layer suturing, and shorter inter-pregnancy interval were identified as independent risk factors for uterine rupture, with their combined assessment providing high predictive accuracy (AUC=0.894).
mod_finding: Single-layer cesarean suturing in a previous birth was identified as an independent risk factor for uterine rupture in subsequent deliveries.
